title: The monochrome series — the second solution
why: Colour left the imagery layer. The hue-bearing series in series.json is kept as the record of how it was solved, and as what a DATA PLOT may still reach for; nothing else uses it.
whyNotZeroChroma: A true zero-chroma grey is cold, and this system's ground is warm broken white. Same argument as the shadow, which is tinted with --ink's rgb rather than black. At c = 0.0055 the hue is imperceptible: black to grey in practice, warm-neutral by construction.
whyOneStep: The hue-bearing series needed two different steps, 0.127 light and 0.152 dark, because lightness was being traded against hue. Lightness is now the only channel, so one step serves both bands.
supersedes: A first pass borrowed --ink, --ink-secondary and --ink-tertiary for the three layers. It failed: the dark band's second-to-third step measured 0.0810, under the 0.10 floor. The ink ladder is solved for TEXT against a ground, not for three fills against each other.
threeNotFourStillHolds: The cap was never about hue. A fourth series collapsed into its neighbour once desaturated; a monochrome series IS the desaturated case, so the test is passed by construction. At step 0.155 a fourth would still leave 0.155 — but the cap stays, because the figure it serves has three layers and a fourth token with no consumer is the dead value this system polices.
